title: Booze, drugs caused death, coroner finds
article: A Prince George man who died while being arrested at Parkwood Place mall last year succumbed from a lethal dose of cocaine, a coroner's inquest heard Monday.

The drug sent Darrell Raymond Paquette into heart failure which soon killed him, said Dr. James McNaughton, who performed the autopsy. High levels of alcohol and another drug only made Paquette's condition worse, he testified.

Toxicology tests found an alcohol level of .28 -- almost four times the legal driving limit -- and enough codeine, an ingredient found in Tylenol 3, to kill someone by itself, the five-member jury heard.

Paquette, 43, died on the evening of Sept. 27, 2002 after he was arrested for causing a disturbance inside The Bay. The inquest heard he tumbled down the escalator while fleeing from store employees and struggled as staff and an off-duty police officer tried to restrain him. Efforts to revive him with CPR were unsuccessful.

A coroner's inquest must be held whenever someone dies in police custody or while they're being arrested. Unlike a criminal trial, the jury doesn't assign blame but tries to determine how the person died and whether the death could have been prevented. Jurors can also recommend ways to prevent future incidents.

McNaughton also testified "there were a large number of bruises and abrasions to the body" caused by "blunt force trauma" or blows to the body from some impact, either from being struck by something or from banging against objects. But none of the blows individually or taken as a whole could have killed Paquette, he said.

McNaughton said he doesn't believe being wrestled down or restrained contributed to the irregular heart beat that killed Paquette. He added it's possible Paquette could have survived if medical treatment were available immediately.

Toxicologist Dr. Stuart Huckin said lab tests show Paquette had been drinking and smoking crack cocaine shortly before his death, and indicate he had taken Tylenol 3, which contains the drug codeine, that morning. The combination of cocaine, which is a stimulant, and alcohol and codeine, which are depressants that slow bodily functions, along with the high levels of the drugs could have proven lethal, he said.

Michael Gomez, who was working at The Bay the evening Paquette died, testified he was outside on his break when he saw a man walking toward the store, grunting and swearing occasionally. "He also had his hand on his chest as if he was very winded or had chest pains, perhaps," he said.
Gomez said a store manager followed the man up the escalator and he heard movement upstairs for a couple of minutes before he saw Paquette at the bottom of the escalator.

Paquette got up quickly and fled when a manager told him to leave, he said, and he later saw Paquette lying on his stomach with the off-duty police officer, the store manager, and a security guard holding him down. Soon after, Gomez said he was told to run for a first aid kit.
More than 25 witnesses are scheduled to testify at the inquest, which is expected to last nine days.
